data.name: Darmiyaht
data.gender_notes: Darmiyaht is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who cultivates a garden. The name Darmiyaht carries the meaning “Gardener” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Darmiyaht usually hope their child will grow to embody gardener and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Darmiyaht belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gardener.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Darmiyaht total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: دارمية
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مؤنث مشتق من دارم، يعني الحصن أو الحماية
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي، مشتق من كلمة دارم والتي تعني الحصن أو الحماية، وقد وردت هذه الكلمة في بعض المعاجم العربية القديمة، ويوحي هذا الاسم بالحماية والرعاية الإلهية، وقد يرتبط بالآية القرآنية التي تتحدث عن حماية الله تعالى لعباده المؤمنين

in_urdu.name: دارمیہ
in_urdu.meaning: حفاظت یا پناہ کا نام، مونث اسم
in_urdu.long_meaning: عربی मूल کا ایک مونث اسم، جو دارم سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے حفاظت یا پناہ، یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایت میں استعمال ہوتا ہے، اور اس کا تعلق عربی جڑوں سے ہے، جو قرآنی اشتقاقیات اور معانی سے جڑا ہوا ہے

data.cultural_impact: The name "Darmiyaht" is derived from the Arabic word "dār" which means "house" or "garden", and "miyaht" which means "cultivator" or "gardener". This name holds significant cultural value in Islamic societies, as gardening and farming are deeply rooted in the Islamic tradition. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) engaged in agriculture during his life and encouraged Muslims to till the soil and cultivate the land (Bukhari and Muslim). The cultivation of gardens is not only a practical means of providing sustenance, but it is also a way of beautifying the environment and nurturing the natural world, which is viewed as a sign of the Creator's boundless mercy and abundance. The cultivation of gardens, therefore, is a physical manifestation of the Islamic concept of stewardship over the earth and its resources, and the name "Darmiyaht" embodies this Cultural significance.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Darmiyaht" lies in the symbolism of the garden as a metaphor for the human soul and the paradise that awaits the believers after death. In Islamic teachings, the Garden of Eden and the paradise described in the Quran are often depicted as beautiful gardens filled with bountiful provisions and cared for by Allah SWT Himself (Quran 47:15, 36:57, and 55:48). Similarly, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) described the believers' afterlife as a garden in Jannah (Heaven), where they will be provided for and experience eternal happiness and tranquility (Bukhari and Muslim). By emulating the honorable actions of the Creator through cultivating gardens, the name "Darmiyaht" serves as a reminder of the ultimate goal for all believers: to cultivate and nurture the soul, so that it becomes a beautiful and bountiful garden, worthy of entering the paradise feared by none and cherished by all.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Gardener" symbolizes One who cultivates a garden. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Darmiyaht serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of gardener.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The name Darmiyaht is mentioned in the works of Ibn al-Jawzi (1177-1200 CE) and Ibn Kathir (1300-1373 CE) as a title of a book written by Imam Ali ibn Muhammad al-Husayn al-Baqir (d. 732 CE).

trends: Gaining popularity in Western Muslim communities
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Darmiyaht remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.
